title: UpgradeConfig
description: Per-target-repo validation contract at <repo_path>/upgrade.config.json. Confirmed once by the user, then reused deterministically by every run: Stage 4-A's harness and the executor's boot/smoke/test gates are driven by this file, never by per-run guesses.

build_cmd.description: Build command, or null if the repo has no build step.

test_cmd.description: The repo's own test command, e.g. "npm test" or "pytest". Null if the repo has no test suite.

start_cmd.description: Command that boots the application, e.g. "node app.js" or "python app.py".

start_cwd.description: Directory to run start_cmd from, relative to the repo root. Null/omitted means the repo root.

health_url.description: URL polled by boot-smoke.js to decide the app is up, e.g. "http://localhost:3000/".

smoke_routes.description: Routes (paths relative to the health_url origin) requested by the smoke gate; any non-2xx/3xx response fails the gate.

error_strings.description: Optional literal strings whose presence in a smoke-route response body fails the gate (e.g. a template error banner).

services.description: Backing services the app needs, as discovered by Stage 1 analysis — never assumed in advance. Keys are service names (database, cache, queue, search index, ...); values are the provisioning strategy the harness uses: an ephemeral/in-memory provider exercising the real client driver (preferred), "container" for a disposable local instance, "external:<url>" for an existing instance, or "fake" as a last-resort driver-level substitute.

env.description: Environment variables set for boot/test gates, e.g. { "NODE_ENV": "test" }. Connection strings for provisioned services are injected by the harness at runtime under the variable names the app actually reads.
